speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. She recalls attending the state fair over a month ago where she tried various regional foods. Recently, she has observed the darkening of her urine, which she believes is due to inadequate water intake. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed history. Given the dark urine and your history of diabetes, have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, or confusion lately? Also, is there any pain specifically in your right upper abdomen when you take a deep breath?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver_Function_Panel: Total_Bilirubin 3.6 mg/dL, Direct_Bilirubin 2.4 mg/dL, AST 488 U/L, ALT 798 U/L, Alkaline_Phosphatase 72 U/L; CBC: Hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL, Leukocyte_Count 11,600/mm3, Platelet_Count 221,000/mm3; Urinalysis: Not explicitly provided in data.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis A secondary to foodborne transmission from the state fair.

Based on the markedly elevated transaminases (AST/ALT > 1000 range pattern), significant jaundice, and your history of eating regional foods at a fair, this is classic acute viral hepatitis. I recommend imaging of the liver to rule out complications like a gallstone, though the lab picture strongly points to hepatitis.
